changes: Added three lifecycle gates around Proofbound's previously 100%-voluntary shared dev-memory system: (1) a mandatory dev-memory preflight acknowledgement (dev_memory_preflight_ack) required at all four DEV-entry doors (PLAN->DEV, INIT_CHECK->DEV express, and REVIEW/TEST->DEV rollbacks), with a reasoned --reason downgrade path when the preflight build itself fails; (2) a non-blocking advisory reminder appended to finding_resolve output nudging dev_memory_capture when a finding's fix looks like a reusable lesson; (3) a mandatory dev_memory_finish_decision record required before the DONE gate. Includes a core module refactor (finishDecisionPath/readDevMemoryFinishDecision moved to core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts to avoid a core->handlers import), two pre-existing spec-doc reconciliations describing the delivered/escalated behavior, a new 74-assertion smoke test, and 8 collateral fixture fixes for pre-existing tests whose fixtures now also need a satisfying dev-memory artifact.
usage: Run `lattice dev_memory_preflight_ack --storyId=<id>` before a story's first DEV entry (or --reason="<why>" if the preflight pack build itself fails); run `lattice dev_memory_finish_decision --storyId=<id> --decision=captured|no-reusable-lesson|defer-with-reason` before DONE. finding_resolve's output now includes an unconditional dev_memory_capture reminder automatically.
expectedOutcome: A story cannot enter DEV via any door without a recorded preflight ack, cannot reach DONE without a recorded finish-decision, and every resolved finding carries a visible dev-memory capture nudge -- closing the read-before-dev and write-during-dev gaps the user explicitly asked for, while staying inside the existing dev-memory system's non-authoritative-content guarantee (only record EXISTENCE is gate-checked, never lesson content).
actualTranscript: Full 95-command validate suite passes (multiple clean runs). New smoke test: 74/74 assertions pass, covering all four DEV doors refusal-then-pass, the --reason downgrade path, the finding_resolve advisory (including a fail-safe-under-throw case), the DONE-gate decision matrix (all 3 decision values) plus fail-closed corrupt/cross-story-record cases, and a regression test for a genuine bug found and fixed during REVIEW (a fail-open guarantee on the REVIEW/TEST->DEV rollback door was being silently broken by an overly broad internal catch). Three REVIEW lanes (concept/quality/test-coverage) each passed cleanly in round 2 after the fix; full-3x2 cross-host quorum recorded.
outcomeDiff: No gaps between expected and actual. One out-of-role-scope discovery during REVIEW (an unrelated, pre-existing failing test file, proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts, untouched by this diff and not registered in validate.commands) was flagged as a separate follow-up task, not folded into this story.
limitations: Every OTHER currently-active story in this repo will hit CHK-001's new preflight-ack gate the first time it next tries to enter/re-enter DEV, and CHK-003's finish-decision gate the first time it tries to reach DONE -- each is a one-line unblock (dev_memory_preflight_ack / dev_memory_finish_decision) named directly in the refusal message, and this consequence was anticipated and recorded in decision.json's preMortem before implementation began. The immutable per-intentRef evidence-command pin (a pre-existing Lattice mechanism, not something this story built) has no supported way to strengthen or replace an already-pinned weak check discovered during REVIEW; three such cases were resolved via independent manual re-verification recorded in finding_resolve, and this limitation itself was captured as a reusable dev-memory lesson for future stories.
pitfalls: A count-based selector string (e.g. pinning the exact number of assertions a smoke test prints) breaks permanently the next time that test legitimately grows -- CHK-004:happy:0 hit this and had to be waived rather than re-earned. When adding a new check inside an existing gate function, measure the character/byte distance to any downstream AST-sconed contract check (verify-process-fact-contract.mjs enforces a 2500-char window between canFinishGuard's declaration and its evaluateReviewVerdict call) before writing a long explanatory comment. A new gate check added to a rollback door with an existing documented fail-open contract must let genuine I/O faults propagate rather than catching everything -- this exact class of bug was introduced then caught and fixed within this same story.
